title: Docs/examples: add safe streaming retry guidance + sane timeout defaults
author: Wei Chen
release_notes:
- Docs-only: Added troubleshooting guidance for streaming disconnects/timeouts (retry/backoff, idempotency hints, request-id logging).
- Docs-only: Recommended timeout configuration in examples; clarified defaults and how to override per-request.
- Linked to Known Issues article for deeper workaround details.
description: Context: Support is seeing repeat tickets where customers use streaming without explicit timeouts and/or implement unsafe retries (e.g., retrying mid-stream without backoff, or treating disconnects as hard failures). This PR updates the Python SDK docs and examples to make the safe path obvious and copy/paste-friendly, aligned with the escalation/known-issues sprint. What changed: (1) Added a dedicated “Streaming: retries, timeouts, and reconnects” section with concrete patterns: retry only when the stream fails before completion; use exponential backoff with jitter; treat client timeouts separately from server disconnects; log/capture request IDs for Support. (2) Updated examples to show explicit timeout configuration (connect/read) and a recommended baseline for production. (3) Added links to the Known Issues article “Streaming timeouts and reconnect” so Support can reference a single canonical workaround page. (4) Added a small note on idempotency: if the caller may retry, they should provide stable inputs and handle duplicated partial output (client-side) rather than assuming the server will resume. Out of scope: changing SDK runtime behavior or default timeouts in code; this is docs/examples only. References: SUP-1842 (streaming resets, us-east) and SUP-1854 (truncated streams) and Linear ENG-4827. Validation: docs build + example lint; no runtime changes.
commits: docs(streaming): add retry/backoff + timeout guidance section
examples: configure client timeouts and request-id logging in streaming sample
docs: link known-issues article + add ‘when to escalate’ callout
chore: fix formatting/lint and doc anchors
changed_files: examples/streaming_chat.py (explicit timeouts; retry wrapper; request-id logging)
tests/test_examples_smoke.py (adjusted to reflect new example args)
review_conversation: Elliot Price (Docs): Please add a clear ‘When to escalate to Support’ callout and avoid implying the SDK guarantees resume semantics. Wei Chen (Author): Added a callout block with the same language as the Known Issues article; clarified ‘no resume’ and client responsibility for dedupe. Priya Shah (Support): Can we make request-id capture more prominent? This is the #1 reason we go back-and-forth. Wei Chen: Updated both examples to print/record x-request-id when available and added a short snippet for customers to paste into tickets. Rafael Mendes (SRE): Timeout guidance should separate connect vs read; also avoid recommending disabling HTTP/2 here (that belongs in KB where it’s caveated/temporary). Wei Chen: Split timeout into (connect, read) in examples and removed HTTP/2 mention from SDK docs; left that mitigation only in the KB link. Owen Phillips (Support Incidents): Add a note about retries on 429/503 being different from stream disconnects. Wei Chen: Added a paragraph distinguishing transport disconnects vs server rejections (429/503) and points to rate-limit troubleshooting. Approvals: Elliot + Priya approved after second revision; Rafael approved after timeout wording change.
